header.business: Example Roasters, an online coffee roaster (invented example)
header.product: House Blend whole bean coffee, 340 g bag

rules: blank or non-numeric price answer: removed from Van Westendorp
a price above 5x or below 0.2x that question's median: removed from Van Westendorp
answers out of order (too cheap <= bargain <= getting expensive <= too expensive): removed from Van Westendorp
ladder intent rising 2+ points as price rises, or a blank rung: removed from Gabor-Granger

excluded.reason: implausible price (above 5x or below 0.2x the question median)
contradictory order (too cheap above getting expensive)
ladder intent rises with price, or a blank rung

van_westendorp.reading: Few respondents reject a bag between $14.42 and $19.85. The optimal price point ($16.25) is where as many call it too cheap as too expensive; the indifference point ($18.02) is where as many call it a bargain as expensive. These are perceptions, not purchases, so the ladder below picks the price.

segments.van_westendorp: too few answers to price separately
segments.gabor_granger: too few answers to price separately

sales_elasticity.method: before and after with a control: ln((Q after / Q before) / (C after / C before)) / ln(P after / P before)
sales_elasticity.Q: full-price House Blend units per 1,000 sessions, daily mean
sales_elasticity.C: units of every other coffee per 1,000 sessions, daily mean

unadjusted_read.how: all units per day including promo orders, no traffic or control
unadjusted_read.why_not_used: the LABORDAY15 promo orders and a store-wide September rise in units bought per session (other coffees up 7.3% per 1,000 sessions, while sessions moved only 1.1%) hide most of the price effect

recommendation.rule_1_profit_rung_inside_range: Profit peaks at $18 (364.6 per 100 respondents against 363.2 at $16), inside the $14.42 to $19.85 range.
recommendation.rule_2_sales_check: The move from $14 to $16 measured -0.66 (95% interval -0.92 to -0.40): inelastic, so a further rise is supported.
recommendation.rule_3_rival_check: $18 sits inside the range with 2 of 3 rivals above it per 340 g.
recommendation.margin_over_current: Close call: the profit index at $18 is 0.4% above $16 while survey demand is 18.5% lower, so the survey alone can't settle it; the sales check and the test decide.
recommendation.segment_note: Profit peaks by segment: subscribers $18, one-time buyers $18. New visitors were too few to price. At $18, one-time buyers lose the most survey demand (17.6% fewer buyers per 100 than at $16); read their conversion separately in the test.
recommendation.survey_vs_sales: The survey ladder implies an arc elasticity of -1.74 from $16 to $18, against -0.66 measured in real orders on the $14 to $16 move. Stated intent overstates price sensitivity here, so plan on the sales figure and treat the survey as the outer bound of the risk.
recommendation.test_plan: Run $18 against $16: a clean before and after with the other coffees as control, at least 14 days and 30 full-price orders per side, with no promotion codes running. Expect full-price units per 1,000 sessions to change by about -7.5% (between -10.3% and -4.7% on the interval).
